catalog_quote: [Pavlík 2017: 37] Each word has its distinctive tone, however the tone can be reduced and influenced by surrounding words and overall intonation, therefore the tone curve is very unstable ... There are six possible tone contours, but we have found at most only four exact words pronounced in different tone contour, therefore there may be only four tonemes. ... [Nishida 2013: 39] Nàmùyì is a tone language with different pitch variation on a syllable or phonological word to convey meaning. ... Nàmùyì speakers control the pitch of the voice (its relative highness or lowness) to effect a variation of F0, hence producing lexically contrastive tones. ... [Nishida 2013: 49] In Nàmùyì polysyllabic words, a slightly heavier stress most often falls on the initial syllable of the root, regardless of the overall phonotactic structure of the phonological word. audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: all three tagged portions of the deciding quotation are present verbatim at the stated places in copies we hold (Pavlík p.37 in the extracted text; Nishida p.39 and p.49 on the page images we hold, scanned text matching modulo noise). (2) Deciding sources are a 2017 PhD descriptive grammar (Pavlík, western Namuzi) plus a 2013 phonology article (Nishida, eastern/Dzolo), both open and. both call the language tonal, and Nishida's weak root-initial stress tendency is already carried in the secondary-stress rule with the Gurung-template caveat. (3) The one clearly superior unheld work on Glottolog's list, Li (Lakhi) 2017 La Trobe PhD (726 pp; Glottolog lists it twice under 'Lakhi, Libu' and 'Li, Jianfu' — same thesis), was downloaded now from La Trobe OPAL and read: three contrastive tonemes H/M/L (/54 33 21/) with two sandhi tones, all nine disyllabic tone patterns attested (p.30, p.142, p.275-276)

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: p.30: 'There are three contrastive tonemes — high, middle and low. The high tone is notated as high falling /54/, middle as mid-level /33/ and low as low falling /21/'. p.142: 'Tone is the use of different pitch heights to contrast lexical or grammatical meaning. Tone sandhi is part of the inflectional system'. p.275-276: all nine disyllabic tone combinations attested (54+54 ... 21+21), 16 of 27 trisyllabic. Abstract p.xx: 'Three-way contrastive lexical tone—high, middle and low—plays an important role, with an additional two tones through sandhi processes.' No section or statement on lexical
sources.locator: p.30 (sec. 2, Table 2-4 Tone); ch.3 'Tone and Sandhi' p.142; sec. 3.5 'Tone structure' p.275-276; abstract p.xx; incidental 'stress' only at p.433 (emphatic adjective, last syllable stressed before /ɦa/) and p.705 (vowel after /da³³/ stressed).
sources.note: Largest description of the language (726 pp, native-speaker author, Praat-measured tone chapter); record rested on Pavlík's 206-pp thesis and Nishida's article without it. downloaded now: confirms tonal (3 tonemes + sandhi), silent on word stress.
